statement: Build a one-page website for a coffee shop that lets visitors see the menu with prices, opening hours, the address with a map and how to contact the shop.
audience: Local people and passers-by looking for a coffee shop who want to know what is on offer, when it is open and how to find or contact it.
standards: Tap targets big enough on phones
Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file
rules: Never invent a fact the Requester has not given: address, hours, phone, email, menu items and prices show a visible 'to be confirmed' placeholder until supplied
Where the Requester said to decide, use typical choices for a coffee shop and list each one on the page's assumptions list or in the delivery notes for the Requester to check
No real files of the Requester are touched
visitor_needs: Find the address with a map
charter_items: The page header shows the shop's name and a one-line description of the coffee shop.
The menu section lists drinks and food items, each with a name and a price, and any name or price not yet supplied reads 'to be confirmed'.
The opening hours section shows each day of the week with its hours, and any hours not yet supplied read 'to be confirmed'.
The location section shows the street address and town with a map, and an address not yet supplied reads 'to be confirmed'.
The contact section shows a phone number and an email address, and any not yet supplied read 'to be confirmed'.
The page has one clearly most prominent main action button near the top, which takes the visitor to the location or contact section.
The navigation menu links to every section, and each link scrolls to its section without a broken in-page link.
The page has no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px widths, text is readable against its background, and buttons and links are at least 44px tall to tap on phones.
The page has no JavaScript errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, and every in-page link points to an existing section.
